status: Unapproved visual comparison concepts; not runtime assets or validated animation sheets.
scope: Rapid arrow tower, Longshot bowl catapult and one proposed baseline undead skeleton, in pixel-art and smooth cartoon styles.
provenance: Original generated art for this project. No third-party reference images supplied. The cartoon board is an edit of the original generated pixel-art board.
inputReview: Inspected current Rapid and Longshot Game screenshots, current wood source Game screenshot and original approved Rapid/Longshot project concepts before generating.
notes: Gameplay strips are generated illustrations, not actual Unity screenshots. Additional scenery and heraldic decoration are illustrative and do not define new gameplay or approved lore. Existing 3D scene and gameplay have not been modified. No final pipeline switch has been approved.

images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a visual approval board for original 2D SPRITE art, not a production spritesheet, for an isometric fantasy tower-defense game with manual resource gathering.
Primary request: Create one polished landscape approval image titled exactly "A — PIXEL ART". Show a coherent set of TWO DIFFERENT TOWERS and ONE BASELINE UNDEAD enemy. The point is to judge whether beautiful, readable sprites can be produced directly, without translating the drawings into 3D models. Everything must be original.
Layout: wide 3:2 canvas. Upper 60 percent: three balanced showcase columns, understated cool gray-green flat background, exact short labels "RAPID", "LONGSHOT", "UNDEAD". Left a complete Rapid tower; center a complete Longshot catapult; right a complete undead foot soldier with two smaller alternate-facing walking poses of THAT SAME unit beneath it. Clear spacing, no cropped feet or roof, no elaborate frames. Bottom 35 percent: one small illustrative gameplay fragment using the SAME designs in their proper relative scale, the two towers on a gray stone invasion area edged by green grass, four copies of the one undead walking toward the defenses. Small text above the strip exactly "GAMEPLAY SCALE". This strip is an art mockup, not a claim to be a real game capture.
Camera: consistent fixed orthographic isometric / high three-quarter view looking down about 45 degrees, visible roofs and feet; all ground footprints align to one diamond grid. Towers stand upright. Identical camera for all assets and the small scene.
RAPID identity: tall compact timber watchtower on four thick wooden posts and small pale stone footings, strong cross-braces, open railed platform, warm wood and muted red layered hipped roof with slightly curved eaves and dark metal bands. No archer or human on the platform. A small visible arrow-firing aperture beneath the roof suggests its role. Clear airy silhouette with readable gaps, designed for sprites rather than tiny decorative noise.
LONGSHOT identity: squat stone square foundation, low wood-and-stone parapet, a substantial wooden A-frame with one long spoon/cup catapult arm and a single gray boulder in its bowl. Warm timber and iron bindings. Bowl visible at the top; stable balanced construction, distinct from the taller red-roof Rapid. Not a ballista, trebuchet, cannon or tower with a roof.
UNDEAD identity: ONE proposed baseline skeleton foot soldier, oversized readable ivory skull with dark eye sockets and tiny dim red eyes, intact stylized bony limbs, torn desaturated teal tunic and dark brown belt, slightly hunched purposeful walking posture, empty hands. No gore, weapon, shield or magical boss equipment. Enemy height at gameplay scale about one third to two fifths of Rapid's height. Show the same design in all poses; do not imply new enemy roles.
Style/medium: excellent genuine pixel art, explicit deliberate square pixel clusters and stepped edges throughout, controlled limited color ramps, expressive readable silhouettes, consistent upper-left light. The tower source sprite would be about 96 to 128 pixels high and the enemy about 40 to 48 pixels high; show enlarged pixel clusters in the showcase and small readable sprites in the scene. Integer-like sharp pixel enlargement, no blur, no smooth gradients, no anti-aliased vector edges. Rich but disciplined modern indie pixel art, atmospheric but legible, not low-effort 8-bit icons.
Avoid: 3D render, polygon model appearance, photorealism, painterly smudging, over-detailed noisy outlines, copied commercial game assets, copyrighted characters, UI panels, health bars, invented gameplay systems, extra tower types, extra enemy types, trees obscuring assets, tiny unreadable text, watermarks. Keep the complete board aesthetically consistent.

No pixel edges, pixel fonts, pixel textures or blocky pixel clusters should remain. Do not turn it into a 3D render. Keep objects simple enough to become directly drawn sprites.
